title: Common & Preferred Stock
description: Learn how stock issuances are recorded and understand important differences between common and preferred stock.
html:
Issuing common stock

When a corporation issues shares for cash, cash increases and stockholders' equity increases.

Par value example

A corporation issues 10,000 shares of $1 par common stock for $15 per share.

Cash received

10,000 × $15 = $150,000

Common Stock

10,000 × $1 par = $10,000

Additional Paid-In Capital

$150,000 − $10,000 = $140,000

Preferred stock

Preferred stock can have rights that differ from common stock.

One common feature is a preference regarding dividends.

Cumulative preferred stock

If preferred stock is cumulative, unpaid dividends from prior periods can accumulate as dividends in arrears.

Example

A corporation has 1,000 shares of $100 par, 6% cumulative preferred stock.

Annual Preferred Dividend = 1,000 × $100 × 6% = $6,000

Keep these separate

Par value is not necessarily the market price of the stock.

Issue price determines the total cash received in a cash issuance.
